question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party, state institutions, and the People's Liberation Army as of mid-2026, with analysts uniformly expecting him to secure a fourth term at the 21st Party Congress in late 2027. Term limits were abolished in 2018, and recent leadership selections have emphasized loyalty to Xi while sidelining potential rivals, leaving no visible successor or factional challenge capable of forcing removal before the market deadline of December 31, 2026. He continues public diplomacy, policy addresses, and elite appointments without signs of health issues or internal fractures that could trigger resignation or ouster. Trader consensus at 95.3% for "No" aligns with this entrenched position and historical patterns of CCP leadership continuity. Low-probability shifts could still arise from a sudden medical event, major elite defection, or unforeseen crisis altering the Politburo balance.
